A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

arterial hypertension is a major factor in the development of renal failure and its prevention and treatment are essential in order to avoid the progression of renal disease and the appearance of renal insufficiencies.

the control of blood pressure is essential in patients with primary renal disease and that the use of ACE-inhibitors may prevent the progression of renal failure in patients with mild-to moderate renal insufficiency.
arterial hypertension is the main cause of chronic renal failure and the main risk factor for the progression of chronic renal insufficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the progression of renal disease may be prevented by a proper treatment of hypertension.
in patients with hypertension, renal insufficiency and proteinuria, ACE-inhibition should be the first line therapy.
arterial hypertension may favour the appearance of a non-diabetic renal failure, through a direct renal effect or through the occurrence of atheromatosis of renal arteries.
